models.title: European three-way model
models.description: Western hunter-gatherers, Anatolian early farmers and Yamnaya steppe herders (Haak et al. 2015).

models.title: European and West Asian four-way model
models.description: Adds early Iranian farmers for ancestry from the Caucasus and Near East (southern Europe, West Asia).

models.title: South Asian three-way model
models.description: Iranian-related farmers, Middle-to-Late Bronze Age steppe herders and an ancestral South Indian proxy (Narasimhan et al. 2019).

archaic_definition: All of the Altai, Vindija and Chagyrskaya Neanderthals that are called carry the allele (at least two called); under 1% in sub-Saharan African reference genomes (at least 100 chromosomes); at least 1% in European, East Asian and South Asian 1000 Genomes samples combined.

group_names.CEU: Utah residents with Northern and Western European ancestry

regions.title: Northern and Northeast China / Japan and Korea
Papua New Guinea, Melanesia and Australia

not_covered: Central Asia (its populations are themselves mixtures of West and East Eurasian ancestry)
Northeast Africa and the Horn of Africa (too few reference genomes)
Polynesia and Island Southeast Asia (too few reference genomes)
Indigenous North America (few reference genomes; most Indigenous American references are from Central and South America)
Jewish diaspora groups (not in the reference set)

validation.file_check: Raw files written in the AncestryDNA, 23andMe, MyHeritage, FamilyTreeDNA, Living DNA and VCF layouts (including a GRCh38 VCF) are read back with every genotype exact.
validation.pca: Genomes reduced to about 95,358 SNPs (a genotyping chip's worth) land a median 0.95% of the map's width from where the same genomes land with all 1.15 million SNPs (168 placements of 84 held-out genomes).
validation.neanderthal: On 84 held-out genomes reduced to chip size, the 95% interval contained the estimate from all 1.15 million SNPs in 100% of cases.
validation.ancient_ancestry: Athanor's qpAdm reproduces ADMIXTOOLS qpAdm [0.524, 0.282, 0.195] with [0.524, 0.282, 0.194] on a well-powered simulation: every weight agrees to within 0.0006 and every standard error to within 0.0003, and both recover the simulated proportions [0.5, 0.3, 0.2] to within 0.024. On simulated populations whose true proportions are known, the fitted proportions were within two standard errors of the truth for all 6 populations (largest deviation 0.152).
validation.continental_ancestry: On 12 simulated genomes mixing two or three continents, built from the chromosomes of reference people left out of the panels whose own ancestry is unambiguous, the proportions were within 1.4 percentage points on average (4.8 at worst); the 95% intervals, which reflect statistical noise only, contained the true value 100% of the time. On genomes built from any reference people, including members of mixed groups, results matched the sources' own compositions within 1.4 points on average. Reference people left out of their panel are assigned on average at least 91% to their own continent; the rest mostly reflects real shared ancestry between neighbouring regions, which is why each region's typical profile is shown. ADMIXTURE's projection mode gives the same proportions to within 0.002.
validation.regional_ancestry: With 80,000 SNPs, people left out of the reference panels are assigned on average 97% to their own region (lowest region 91%); regions that could not be told apart are reported together.
validation.chromosome_painting: On simulated genomes with known ancestry segments, the pair of ancestries was right at 98% of SNPs, and the average confidence the method reported was 99%.
validation.indigenous_american: Detection limit 3.0%. On simulated genomes with known Indigenous American ancestry the proportion was recovered within 2.6 points from 5% upwards; detection rates at 2%, 5% and 10% were 17%, 50% and 100%; 0% of genomes with none, and 8% of left-out East Asian genomes, were reported as having some.
validation.roh: Segments match PLINK 1.9's --homozyg on the same genotypes (total length within 0.0%, overlap at least 1.00), and homozygous stretches of known length inserted into real genomes were found over 100% of their length.
validation.x_ancestry: From X-chromosome SNPs alone, people left out of the reference panels are assigned on average at least 87% to their own continent (people whose autosomes are unambiguous).
